title: HFCL Ltd - 500183 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: HFCL Q4 FY26 revenue rose to Rs 1,824 crore and EBITDA margin to 18.47%, with a Rs 10,159 crore hyperscaler OFC contract and Rs 21,200 crore order book.
summary.overview: HFCL reported its highest-ever quarterly and annual performance, with FY26 consolidated revenue of Rs 4,949 crore (up from Rs 4,065 crore) and PAT of Rs 329 crore (up from Rs 173 crore). Q4 revenue of Rs 1,824 crore grew sharply from Rs 1,211 crore in Q3 and Rs 801 crore a year earlier, with EBITDA margin at 18.47% versus 20.11% in Q3. Management guided FY27 revenue growth of 20-25% and a 3-4% blended EBITDA margin expansion, driven by price realisations, EPC loss reduction and product mix, while announcing a Rs 580 crore preform plant, defence and aerospace acquisition, and a strategic restructuring committee. Management declined to give firm numeric guidance on several items.

segments.name: Telecom products (incl. OFC)
segments.commentary: Management cited Q4 telecom product revenue of about Rs 901 crore with Rs 361 crore PBT (analyst figures); consolidated telecom products revenue of Rs 1,206 crore at 31.75% margin in Q4 per CFO. FY26 telecom products revenue cited by analyst at Rs 2,931 crore with Rs 764 crore PBT.

segments.name: EPC / turnkey
segments.commentary: Loss-making in recent quarters due to Army network warranty-period costs with no customer receipts; management expects AMC (about Rs 170 crore per year) to be signed around Q2 FY27 to offset losses. BharatNet EPC projects now profitable. Unbilled revenue rose from about Rs 300 crore to Rs 600 crore YoY, partly due to pending invoicing compliances.

segments.name: Defence
segments.commentary: Standalone defence order book about Rs 300 crore; with the aerospace business being acquired (export order book about Rs 1,930 crore) it rises to about Rs 2,230 crore. FY27 defence revenue guided at about 10-12% of revenue, roughly Rs 500-600 crore, with defence margins expected a couple of percentage points above current levels (about 20-25%).

segments.name: Data centre interconnect (HTL Ltd subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Expected to add about Rs 400 crore revenue in FY27 (management said could be Rs 400-500 crore) and about Rs 800 crore in FY28; capacity to be increased multi-fold. Blended margin expected around 20%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of 20-25% year on year, implying about Rs 6,000-6,250 crore on a Rs 5,000 crore base; management said this is conservative and not formal guidance.
Blended EBITDA margin expansion of 3-4 percentage points in FY27, dependent on price realisations, EPC loss reduction and mix; management said multi-year repeat of such expansion is not feasible.
Margin improvement expected to start from Q1 FY27 per management, with EPC losses expected to ease from Q2 FY27 once Army NFS contract converts to AMC.
FY27 total capex about Rs 600 crore; FY28 capex about Rs 350 crore.
Aspiration to reach Rs 10,000 crore revenue in three to five years; no profit guidance given for FY27 (declined analyst's Rs 800-900 crore PAT scenario).
capex_capacity: Optical fibre capacity to rise from 28 mn fkm to 33.9 mn fkm by December 2026; optical fibre cable capacity from 34 mn fkm to 39 mn fkm by July 2026 and 42.36 mn fkm by December 2026.
Management said optical fibre capacity utilisation is 100%, aiming for 110% through productivity measures.

Preform manufacturing facility of about 300 tonnes per year (vs current requirement about 1,000 tonnes per year), estimated capex about Rs 580 crore, expected to take at least 2 years; claimed 15-20% cost saving on preform; possible scale-up to 500 tonnes later.
Ammunition facility in Andhra Pradesh on 1,000 acres; foundation stone planned for May 15, 2026. FY27 budget about Rs 125 crore for this facility, with about Rs 250 crore over the next two years.
Two new IBR machines under installation with more ordered for installation within calendar 2026.
demand_pricing: Management cited 100-150 million fibre km of incremental global demand from hyperscale data centres and AI, concentrated in high fibre count and low-latency cables where supply is constrained.
Average realisations improved significantly; management said FY27 realisation uplift of about 25% is expected, driven by mix and recent price increases over the last 1-2 months.
Management personally expects prices to be near their final level, with only a few percent further increase.
Preform long-term contracts (about 5-6 month repricing per management) are expected to pass on preform cost increases; management said price increases can be passed through in full.

Order book Rs 21,200 crore: about Rs 18,000 crore product deliveries (within one to five years) and about Rs 3,500 crore AMC contracts over 6-7 years. USD 1.1 billion (Rs 10,159 crore) global OFC contract to execute from end of Q1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Could FY27 revenue reach Rs 8,000 crore and PAT exceed Rs 800-900 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to guide to that level but said revenue should grow at least 20-25% over FY26, with a possible 3-4 percentage point blended margin increase.

qa_highlights.question: Is HFCL demerging the project business, and what is the timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: A strategic restructuring committee has been formed to evaluate mergers or demergers across defence, EPC and fibre; no decision or timeline given, and it will report back when a decision is taken.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EPC turn loss-making and why are unbilled revenues rising?
qa_highlights.answer: Losses stem from Army network warranty costs with no customer receipts; AMC (about Rs 170 crore per year) is expected to be signed around Q2 FY27. CFO said part of unbilled revenue is due to OFC invoices and pending compliances, to be invoiced in April-May 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Q4 margin movement be explained, and why did sequential blended margin dip?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cable margins rose but EPC Army-contract costs without revenue caused a minor decline; margins expected to rise in Q1 FY27. Telecom product PBT margin cited at about 31.75% in Q4 on consolidated basis (Rs 1,206 crore revenue), with CFO saying this is not guaranteed going forward.

qa_highlights.question: What is the defence and aerospace acquisition rationale and sequencing?
qa_highlights.answer: Acquisition adds aerostructure and aerospace capabilities with certifications and export order book of about Rs 1,930 crore; definitive agreements to be executed by May 31, 2026, closing within the calendar year. Electronic fuze is undergoing upgrades for DRDO re-evaluation; BMP upgraded sample due June 26, 2026.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Rs 21,200 crore order book is export and what is IBR's share of OFC revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Export orders are Rs 12,250 crore (58%). Management declined to give exact IBR revenue share but said it is a major part of OFC revenue and expected to stay above 50%.

risks_watch: Preform and raw material price inflation (helium and polymers about 20% of cable cost) and the timing of long-term contract repricing.
Execution and margin delivery of the USD 1.1 billion OFC contract from end of Q1 FY27 and the Army AMC conversion in Q2 FY27.
Receivables above Rs 2,000 crore and unbilled revenue of about Rs 600 crore; split by EPC and age not disclosed.
Outcome of the strategic restructuring committee on possible demerger of defence, EPC or fibre businesses, and the Rs 555 crore promoter warrant issue subject to approvals.
Defence programme approvals (BMP upgrade, electronic fuze re-testing, Multi-mode hand grenade tender) and the Andhra Pradesh facility timeline.
Geopolitical and supply-chain shocks, which management said have not yet materially affected production.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth and order book, but consistently hedged on numbers, repeatedly declining formal guidance and citing unknown geopolitical risk. Evasive on per-fibre-km realisation, receivables breakup and IBR revenue share, citing commercial confidentiality.

I would not like to give such a guidance at this point of time. But I can definitely say that over and above the revenue we have achieved in last financial year, we should definitely be able to scale it up by 20% to 25% at least.
Every year, you cannot have 3% to 4% increase. That is impossible. Nobody can do it.
Look, as far as capacity utilization of fiber-optic optical fiber is concerned, it is 100%. We are trying to increase the production by doing various optimal innovative things

But again, as I said 3 times on this call, sir, I cannot put a number now because in the last few months, the type of cable has changed so much with hyperscalers and all that buying cable from 800 fiber to 7,000 fiber and telcos buying 2 fiber to 288 fiber and different kind of constructions.

growth.why: Management guides FY27 revenue growth of 20-25% (midpoint 22.5%) and 3-4 pt blended margin expansion, backed by optical fibre capacity rising 28 to 33.9 mn fkm by Dec 2026 at 100% utilisation, a Rs 10,159 crore USD 1.1bn hyperscaler OFC contract executing from end Q1 FY27, and Rs 21,200 crore order book; pricing uplift of ~25% is expected but firm numeric guidance on several items was declined.
